decision: Every Rust tool in the commons declares its invocation surface - arguments and environment - with argenv, the commons' own crate: ocoeco, tad, the engine, devlab and tone move from clap, one at a time, proven equal (the same commands and environment behaviour).
why: The author asked whether all our tools use argenv; only lab-agent and snapall did. clap was chosen by default without looking inside the commons first; argenv gives one declared, typed, machine-readable contract for argv and env, readable by agents and by ocoeco.
rejected: Keeping clap (a second way to declare a surface, and environment read by hand).

decision: There is not one observatory. OCO is the ecosystem - the agreement (ocoeco) and its tools - that lets anyone have one. A constellation has its own fulldome; an observatory is someone's place where the fulldomes they care about come together, and observatories can be brought together, one gathering others. Observer and observatory named one thing: observatory is kept. The author's observatory - where his own constellations come together - is one of many, to be parted from OCO the ecosystem, with which it is mixed today in one organization. Refined the same day by 2026-11-12-places-lenses-acts: observer is kept after all, as the part of ocoeco that observes - an act, not a place.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: the point of OCO is that it is not one observatory; anyone will be able to create theirs, and all or some can be brought together to share their views of the sky; OCO as a project had got mixed with his own projects. An observatory that can gather others needs no special home above it - the same thing, nested, as Ostrom found lasting commons to be.
rejected: One observatory for everyone (a centre the commons would then depend on); a special home of observers above observatories (an observatory gathering others is enough); two words, observer and observatory, for one thing; parting the author's observatory from the ecosystem at once (a careful move, later).

decision: oco- before a name marks a star of OCO itself (oco-agent). -oco after a name marks a place someone made with OCO - a constellation or an observatory alike (linux-phone-oco, marshall-oco). The name says made with OCO; the mark says what kind of place it is.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: OCO's stars are named with oco preceding; the observatories others make with OCO end in -oco; the author's own observatory has its organization, marshall-oco.
rejected: A different ending for constellations and for observatories (the mark already says the kind, and a name that says it twice can say it wrongly).

decision: OCO is three kinds of things. Places, where data lives (git repositories today): a star produces; a constellation is a family of stars that belong together, gathering their data and keeping what holds between them; an observatory is someone's looking, gathering what they care to see. Ways of seeing: a lens - the data it needs, where it comes from, how it is shown - made once and used by anyone; and the fulldome, the outermost lens, the same for every place over whatever it holds. Acts of ocoeco: record (a star producing its data where things are fresh), observe (the observer: gathering from other places, the same at every scale) and show (running lenses). The observer brings data and the names of lenses; since a lens shows the same data the same way anywhere, taking a ready render is a shortcut, not a principle.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: star, constellation and observatory come from the need for places; without the constellation the relations between projects have nowhere to live; the fulldome is the board taken to its full potential, realized in ocoeco's structure and lenses; a lens, once done, just works for anyone in ocoeco; the observer finds its place in ocoeco as what allows the gathering of gatherings. Sorting the words by kind shows the same shape at every scale (the-same-at-every-scale).
rejected: Star and observatory alone (belonging and looking are different claims: one about the stars, one about the looker); the fulldome as one lens beside the others (it would no longer be the whole); the fulldome as something other than a lens (a second mechanism); observer as a second word for observatory (2026-11-12-many-observatories is refined: it is an act of ocoeco, not a place); a lens that must bring its own instruments (a plugin system); observatories gathering only renders (a view of the whole needs the data).

decision: The whole is called the fulldome, not the room, and it has no walls: a part of it is a lens, and what is connected - a decision, its research, the work it caused, the result - is seen as connected. The fulldome shows the story (why a star exists, what it must reach, how, what is happening), time (the sky on any date: the data's own history) and intent, and it is touched and acted in, not watched. What a lens and a render are is not a protocol beside ocoeco: it is ocoeco - the shared language and the mark grow to say them, and ocoeco's tools read, check and write them, so a star follows the agreement by using ocoeco, not by remembering it.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: room and wall do not fit the whole; a planetarium's dome shows not only constellations but the story behind them, relations, a history, intent; and ocoeco is the agreement and a convenient way to follow it automatically - not principles on paper, a ritual, or a discipline in someone's head. Fulldome belongs with star, constellation, lens, observer and observatory; a dome is one continuous sky, where walls divide.
rejected: Room and wall (2026-11-12-the-room keeps its substance; its words are replaced); a render agreement as a protocol of its own (rules to read and remember: the thing ocoeco exists to make unnecessary); a fulldome one only watches (a planetarium's audience: the open commons' must invite).

decision: A board is the room, not a list: the open commons' obeya, where anyone sees the whole. ocoeco's entities are its walls, and a wall is a lens. OCO is described by four words: a star (one idea or project keeping its own ocoeco data), a constellation (stars seen together), a lens (queries and how they are shown, over the same data), an observer (gathers renders, renders nothing of others again); OCO is the home of observers. The flow of work built as ocoeco board is one lens of the room, not the room. A view across stars is a lens of their constellation, rendered once there from the stars' data, so observers still only gather renders; and a render carries a small agreement - its lens, its format, where it starts - so an observer can place it. Lenses declared as data replace three things planned apart: the renderer leaving tad, presentation as data, and the observatory engine's hand-written views. Its words are replaced the same day by 2026-11-12-the-fulldome: the whole is the fulldome, and a part of it is a lens, not a wall.
why: The author, 2026-11-12: ocoeco is the next step, for open commons, of the room where everyone sees the whole - as a principle, a system and an implementation - learnt by seeing and touching, not by cramming; too much had been centred on the backlog; and words are added only where they reflect the whole and make it simpler. The research (the-room) shows the walls are already here, and that the author's four words and the room are one design.
rejected: The board as a view over the backlog alone (one wall taken for the room: 2026-11-12-the-board is refined by this); a board entity of its own; observers rendering stars' data themselves (a star owns how it is shown, and no star may need an observer to be seen); a framework's ceremonies and score boards; adding words that name no distinct part of the whole.

decision: OCO is a constellation in a place of its own - open-commons-observatory/ecosystem - gathering ocoeco, ocoeco-engine, tad and lab-agent (oco-agent). The author's observatory is in its own organization - marshall-oco/marshall-oco.github.io, published at marshall-oco.github.io - gathering his nine organizations, OCO among them as one constellation. Both were made by ocoeco init --gathers and observe only what they gather. The first observatory, in OCO's organization, is untouched and stays until the author's stands where it does.
why: OCO is the ecosystem, not an observatory (2026-11-12-many-observatories); the author, 2026-11-13: my observatory tracks the OCO constellation itself. Until now the observatory's site, its harvest and its data lived in OCO's organization, so OCO looked like one person's observatory.
rejected: The name open-commons-observatory/oco for OCO's place: it is the old name of the engine's repository and GitHub still redirects it - a new repository there would destroy the redirect, and any clone still pointing at it would talk to another repository unknowingly; that cannot be undone, where renaming ecosystem later keeps a redirect. Moving the first observatory at once (nothing public breaks on the way). The observatory's repository as OCO's place (it holds the first observatory's own records).
